missionPremise: G-90 merged shell function parity into smartcity-dashboards at c7d7980 and the kit went on vendoring ecfae70, so vendor/shell.css, vendor/index.html and vendor/app.js were all stale copies. The G-90 lane's conclusion that no kit re-vendor was owed is correct about the PRODUCT-LINE question and wrong about this one: sc-kit.css is byte-identical across three repos and a token change there forks the system, but the kit vendors BOTH stylesheets, stylesheetClasses() counts across both, and vendor-parity arm B byte-compares against whatever smartcity-dashboards main is at the moment CI runs. So the kit's SHIPPED.size === 139 pin was passing on a stale file, which is a gate being lied to rather than a gate holding. The premise was not taken on trust: it was WATCHED FAILING on the untouched clone at d6bd9a1 before anything was edited, 80 pass / 1 fail, the failure being arm B naming vendor/shell.css. Sources: the compiled dispatch _dispatches/2026-08-19_t1kit_dispatch.md, the worked precedent close _inbox/2026-08-19_b8845_close.json (kit PR #7, 109 to 139 by this same chain), and the product's own G-90 shell.css block at c7d7980, whose comment states the rule the wrap had to hold.

Run `npm run refresh:vendor -- <a smartcity-dashboards checkout at c7d7980>` and see zero files change. Run `SC_DASHBOARDS_DIR=<that checkout> npm test` and get 86 of 86 with nothing skipped, including the coverage assertion that every one of the 143 classes is emitted by some component. Run `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:examples` and get exit 0. Run `npm run prove:gates` and see 34 of 34 injections fire and name their file plus 1 of 1 control stay green. Read test/gate3-classes.test.mjs and find the coverage assertion unweakened, with no exclusion set and no class parked as structural. Read src/shell.tsx and find PopItem carrying no disabled prop. The CI check-run conclusion string on the head SHA is "success" and the run log contains both `ok 85 - arm B` and `arm B ran`.
scopeBasis: The dispatch drew the boundary at a green PR and stopped short of the merge and of the DesignSync upload, both planner-owned, so neither is here. Inside that boundary the executable question was which classes get wrapped, and the answer is all four with no exclusion set, because the dispatch named that explicitly as the failure mode to avoid. Four things were deliberately excluded rather than forgotten. vendor/sc-kit.css was not touched and did not move in the refresh, because a token change there is a product-line decision across three byte-locked repos and not a kit PR. ds-bundle/, .ds-sync/ and .render-check.json were not rebuilt or modified; none exists in a fresh clone, so nothing was wiped either. No parity case was added for an OPEN popover or for an available PopItem, because the product ships neither: both popovers ship closed and all seven shipped pop-items are unavailable, and a case with no product counterpart is a case that cannot fail for the right reason. And harness/render-harness.mjs was NOT given a sixth gallery page, because its last part deliberately runs to GALLERY.length so a new component cannot fall off the bottom, and at 86 entries part 5 carries six. Two things were included beyond the literal ask and are named rather than buried: three markup-parity cases with a small widening of the markup instrument to make one of them possible, and a paragraph in .design-sync/conventions.md, which ships verbatim into the README uploaded to the Design project and whose Shell section would otherwise have told the design agent that the top bar carries city, environment, search and identity and nothing else.

components.TopMenu: <div class="topmenu">. No open state and no trigger slot: a trigger prop would have made this a menu widget with opinions about focus, keyboard handling and dismissal, none of which is a class this stylesheet ships, and a package that owns no styling should not grow behaviour it cannot express in the vocabulary it wraps.
components.Pop: <div class="panel pop" role="group" aria-label={label} hidden={!open}>. The pair is emitted rather than offered as a composition, because .pop declares no border, background or radius and a bare .pop renders as an unframed floating block. `label` is required: both shipped instances carry role=group plus an aria-label, and a popover the assistive layer cannot name is a panel for sighted users only. `open` defaults to CLOSED.
components.PopItem: available arm is <button type="button" class="pop-item">; unavailable arm is the same button with disabled plus a sibling <span class="basis">. There is NO disabled prop.

theLawThisFamilyCarries.rule: an unavailable entry states why. The product wrote it, not this lane. shell.css at .pop-item[disabled]: 'An unavailable entry reads as unavailable rather than merely unresponsive. Its reason is the .basis line its group carries, filled from the server.' index.html above the block: 'a control that has not yet heard from the server must not look available.'
theLawThisFamilyCarries.howHeld: by removing the escape hatch, not by review. `disabled` is removed from the prop bag with Omit<ButtonBase, "disabled">, and `unavailable` is not a flag: it IS the basis text. An entry cannot be greyed out without saying why because there is no prop that greys it out. Same technique as ModelCite's Omit<AnchorBase, "children"> at G-88, so this is the established idiom in this package rather than a new one.
heldThreeWays: test/law.test.mjs asserts the Omit is still in source AND asserts the exact rendered output of both arms, so a component that keeps the Omit and stops emitting the basis line also fails
test/consumer.test.mjs MUST_NOT_COMPILE watches the compiler reject <PopItem disabled>Sign in</PopItem> through the packed tarball and the exports map
scripts/prove-gates.mjs gained two injections for this law: one puts the escape hatch back, one drops the basis line. Both watched FIRING.
theLawThisFamilyCarries.secondLaw: Pop is closed by omission. `open = false` is asserted in source and both rendered arms are asserted. A third injection flips the default open and was watched firing. The loudest thing a top bar can do is put a panel over the page, so it must not be one forgotten prop away.

theOneRealDesignDecision.question: the five shipped .pop-group instances are not uniform. Groups 1, 2 and 4 carry ONE trailing basis for the whole group; groups 3 and 5 carry a basis per entry. No single API renders all five byte-for-byte.
theOneRealDesignDecision.chosen: PopGroup's `basis` is OPTIONAL and trailing; PopItem's `unavailable` carries the requirement.
theOneRealDesignDecision.why: the rule the product wrote is about a CONTROL, not about a container. Requiring a group basis would have enforced where a sentence sits and would have made the per-entry form unrepresentable, forcing a second reason line onto every group that already states its reasons row by row.
theOneRealDesignDecision.cost: the shipped group of three unavailable entries sharing one trailing basis renders three basis lines in the kit rather than one. Named rather than buried. Both compositions remain expressible; what is NOT expressible is an unavailable entry with no reason anywhere, which is the point.
theOneRealDesignDecision.whatWasNotDone: no runtime children inspection and no 'this group must contain a basis somewhere' rule. A React component cannot type-check what its siblings render, so that rule would have had to be a review comment, and DEV_PROCESS rule 0 says a control that depends on someone remembering is not a control.
